memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Aaron is to present the Levites before the Lord as a wave offering from the Israelites, so that they may be ready to do the work of the Lord. Then the Levites are to lay their hands on the heads of the bulls, using one for a sin offering to the Lord and the other for a burnt offering, to make atonement for the Levites." - Num 8:11-12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The Levites were presented to God as a "wave offering." Normally a wave offering was something lifted up and waved before the Lord — grain, or a portion of a sacrifice. But here the offering was people. The Levites themselves were the gift, lifted up and given to God for His service.

What a picture this is. God does not merely want our things — our money, our produce, our sacrifices. He wants us. The greatest offering we can bring is ourselves, given wholly to Him.

This is exactly the language the New Testament uses for every believer. Paul urges us: "offer your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and pleasing to God—this is your true and proper worship" (Rom 12:1). We are not called to bring God an offering and then keep our lives to ourselves. We are the offering.

Notice again that atonement was made for the Levites first, through the sacrifices. Only atoned-for people can be offered to God. It is because our sin has been dealt with in Christ that we can now give ourselves to God and be accepted.

Being a "living sacrifice" means our whole life is placed on the altar — not to be consumed, but to be used by God. Every day, we can say, "Lord, here I am. Use me."

Have you given yourself to God as a living offering? Not just your gifts, but you?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Have you offered God your things, but not yourself?
- What does it mean to be a "living sacrifice"?
- How can you place your whole life at God's disposal today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, I offer You not just my gifts but myself. Take my whole life as a living sacrifice, cleansed by Christ and ready to do Your work. Amen.
